proposed.explanation:
Comparison of the four companies on FY2025 vs FY2024 net-profit growth and trailing P/E (price ÷ FY2025 EPS):

• ETEL (Telecom Egypt): Net profit grew from 10,111,328,000 EGP to 22,578,063,000 EGP, a 123.3 % increase. EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93 EGP. At 141.95 EGP the P/E is ≈ 11.9×.
• COMI (CIB): Net profit grew from 55,256,732,000 EGP to 82,258,815,000 EGP, a 48.9 % increase. EPS rose from 14.72 to 18.25 EGP. At 128.00 EGP the P/E is ≈ 7.0×.
• EFID (Edita): Net profit grew from 1,606,727,698 EGP to 2,695,301,670 EGP, a 67.7 % increase. EPS rose from 1.09 to 2.18 EGP. At 20.40 EGP the P/E is ≈ 9.4×.
• TMGH (Talaat Moustafa): Net profit grew from 12,769,517,325 EGP to 18,201,981,482 EGP, a 42.5 % increase. EPS rose from 4.38 to 6.98 EGP. At 82.50 EGP the P/E is ≈ 11.8×.

For a 7+ year growth mandate with medium risk tolerance, ETEL offers the strongest profit-growth signal (123 %) at a P/E (≈ 11.9×) that is not stretched relative to the other three. Telecom is a defensive, cash-flow-rich sector in Egypt, which suits a medium-risk profile. COMI is the cheapest on P/E (7.0×) but its growth is moderate; EFID is a solid middle ground; TMGH has the lowest growth and a P/E similar to ETEL, giving it less of a growth edge.

I recommend buying 281 shares of ETEL at 141.95 EGP = 39,887.95 EGP. This keeps ETEL at ≈ 49.9 % of the 80,000 EGP total portfolio, respecting the 50 % single-position cap, and leaves ≈ 40,112 EGP in cash for future diversification.

Risks and uncertainty: the 123 % profit jump is based on a single fiscal year and may reflect one-time items (e.g., currency revaluation, asset disposals) rather than a sustainable run-rate. We have no revenue, debt, or dividend data to confirm quality. If the growth proves non-recurring, the 11.9× P/E could look rich. Monitor the next two quarterly reports before adding to the position. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
